en.name: Chocolate hazelnut spread
en.summary: Chocolate hazelnut spread keeps to the use-by date printed on the package — there is no separate general figure for it. For best quality, do not refrigerate it and do not microwave it: both ruin the texture that makes it spreadable.
en.pantry: A cool, dark cupboard is the right home, and the honest answer on timing is a rule rather than a number: go by the use-by date on the package, both before and after opening. The spread is an emulsion of sugar, hazelnut, cocoa and vegetable fat with very little water in it, which is why it sits happily at room temperature; what ends a jar in practice is the fat going stale or seizing rather than anything growing in it. Keep it away from the hob and out of direct sun, which soften it and can make the oil separate.
en.fridge: Do not refrigerate it. This is a quality instruction rather than a safety one, but it is a firm one: cold makes the fat set hard, so the spread tears bread instead of spreading on it, and repeated chilling and warming encourages the oil to separate and the sugar to go grainy. A cupboard at ordinary room temperature keeps it smooth. If the jar has become firm because the kitchen is cold, leave it somewhere warmer for an hour rather than warming it in the microwave.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for chocolate hazelnut spread and freezing it is counterproductive. If refrigeration hardens the emulsion, a freezer does so far more thoroughly, and a thawed jar is often grainy with separated oil on top. There is nothing to gain, either: the jar is shelf-stable to its date as it is, and the freezer space is better used on something perishable.
spoilage: A rancid or crayon-like smell from the hazelnut and vegetable fats.
Oil separated into a layer that will not stir back in.
A gritty, grainy texture where it was smooth.
Mould at the surface or around the rim, usually from a wet or used knife.
tips: Use a clean dry knife; crumbs and moisture are what spoil a jar.
Keep it at ordinary room temperature, not in the fridge.
Warm a firm jar in a warm room, not in the microwave.
Do not double-dip a knife that has touched butter or bread crumbs.

faq.q: How long does chocolate hazelnut spread keep?
faq.a: Follow the use-by date printed on the package. No separate general figure is published for it.

faq.q: Should chocolate hazelnut spread be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. For best quality, do not refrigerate or microwave it — cold sets the fat hard and heat separates it.

faq.q: Why has my spread gone grainy?
faq.a: The emulsion has broken, usually after being chilled and warmed repeatedly or heated. It is a texture problem rather than a safety one.

zh.name: 榛果巧克力醬
zh.summary: 榛果巧克力醬請以包裝上印的有效日期為準——它沒有另外的通用數字。為了維持最佳品質，不要冷藏、也不要微波：這兩件事都會毀掉它「抹得開」的質地。
zh.pantry: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃就是對的位置；至於時間，誠實的答案是一條規則而不是數字：開封前後都以包裝上的有效日期為準。這種抹醬是糖、榛果、可可與植物油脂的乳化物，含水量極低，所以它在室溫下很安穩；實務上終結一罐的，是油脂走味或乳化崩解，而不是長了什麼東西。請遠離爐台與陽光直射，那會讓它變軟、也可能讓油分離出來。
zh.fridge: 不要冷藏。這是品質上的指示而非安全問題，但態度很明確：低溫會讓油脂凝硬，抹的時候不是塗開麵包而是把它撕破；反覆冷藏再回溫，也容易讓油分離、糖變得粗糙。放在一般室溫的櫥櫃，它才會保持滑順。如果因為天氣冷而變硬，請把罐子放在溫暖一點的地方一小時，而不是拿去微波。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給榛果巧克力醬的冷凍期限，而且冷凍只會適得其反。既然冷藏就會讓乳化變硬，冷凍只會更徹底，解凍後的罐子常常變得粗糙、表面浮一層油。而且也沒什麼好處：它本來就能常溫放到標示日期，冷凍庫的空間留給容易壞的東西比較划算。
spoilage: 榛果與植物油脂散發油耗味或蠟筆味。
油分離成一層，而且攪不回去。
原本滑順的質地變得粗糙帶顆粒。
表面或罐口長霉，通常來自沾濕或用過的刀。
tips: 用乾淨乾燥的刀；麵包屑和水分才是毀掉一罐的元凶。
放一般室溫，不要放冰箱。
變硬就放到溫暖的房間回溫，不要微波。
沾過奶油或麵包屑的刀不要再插回罐子裡。

faq.q: 榛果巧克力醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 以包裝上印的有效日期為準。它沒有另外公布的通用數字。

faq.q: 榛果巧克力醬要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 不要。為了維持品質，不要冷藏也不要微波——低溫讓油脂凝硬，加熱則讓它分離。

faq.q: 我的抹醬怎麼變得粗粗的？
faq.a: 乳化結構壞了，通常是反覆冷藏回溫或加熱造成的。這是口感問題，不是安全問題。
